tickets.summary: Found 2026-07-13 via api access log during the T-154.1 pause: two editor tabs share the single-use refresh token; tab A rotates it, tab B later POSTs the stale one -> /auth/refresh 401 -> the whole browser session dies (log: 12:13 local, registry+compat 401 -> refresh 401 -> all subsequent 401). Fix: cross-tab mutex around refresh (Web Locks API, BroadcastChannel fallback) + adopt the rotated pair from the winning tab (storage event), so N tabs spend one rotation. Mechanically checked across all five (TBD_MissionBrowser, TBD_BriefingController, TBD_LobbyController, TBD_SpectatorHost, TBD_MarkerController): NO duplicate method names in any two blocks; exactly ONE vanilla override in the whole set (OnControlledEntityChanged, in TBD_MissionBrowser alone) so no two blocks override the same method; and all 20 RplRpc handler names are unique under a consistent TBD_RpcAsk_/TBD_RpcDo_ convention. What remains unprovable on the fast lane is whether the engine MERGES five modded blocks of one class correctly at runtime — world-boot has zero players and every one of these blocks is inert without a client.

T-181.26.notes: REWRITTEN A THIRD TIME — each revision corrected the previous one, and this one rests on a measurement rather than an argument. The premise BOTH earlier versions accepted is FALSE: meta.name, meta.terrain, slot.groupCallsign and slot.role are schema ERRORS when empty (minLength:1, and a pattern on terrain — verified directly in mission.schema.json), not warnings. 'Warning' is only TBD_MissionValidator's RUNTIME severity; the mod validator is strictly MORE PERMISSIVE than the schema that produced the document. So a schema-valid mission can never carry those four empty, and no golden fixture can cover them. THE EXPOSURE IS STILL REAL, for a sharper reason: a document that BYPASSED schema validation can reach the mod. Confirmed at apps/website/api/src/handlers/missions.rs:820 — the /compiled endpoint calls flatten_to_mod_document and serves the result WITHOUT validating it; validate_mission_document exists only inside #[cfg(test)]. The WRITE path is guarded (validate_mission_editor_payload on save at :319 and :587); the READ path that feeds the mod is not. CONSEQUENCE: the mod-side defensive layer is LOAD-BEARING, not redundant. Fix stays as scoped — one sentinel convention across the three wire formats plus pack/sanitise at TBD_SpawnManager.c:577 — but the justification is 'the server can hand us an unvalidated document', not 'a legal mission has empty fields'. See T-181.31 for closing it at the source.

T-181.27.notes: Consume the briefing prose that T-181.23 parsed but nothing reads. Add situation/mission/execution (+markers) to TBD_BriefingPayload, serialise them, and render an ORDERS section in TBD_BriefingScreen via TBD_MissionLoader.GetBriefingForFaction(). This is what makes the briefing screen a BRIEFING rather than a structure dump — the operator named it as an Arma-3 parity feature. Keep side discipline: prose is per-faction and must stay server-filtered like the rest of the payload.

T-181.28.notes: Briefing has no JIP catch-up. T-181.23 deleted the 500ms poll and made it push-only, but NotifyLocalStageUI silently drops the notification when GetPlayerController() is null, and m_TBD_LastStage starts at LOADING per controller. So a client joining/reconnecting while the round sits in BRIEFING may never see it. This is the NORMAL case, not an edge: BRIEFING is admin-driven only, so rounds sit there. The lobby kept its poll and is JIP-safe; the briefing is not. Fix: a catch-up read of GetStage() when the local controller first appears (not a reinstated poll).

T-181.29.notes: Lobby picker opens on top of already-deployed players. Raise() is unconditional by design ('gating the initial open would mean the picker silently never appears'), but m_bAutoDeploy=1 deploys everyone 250ms into LOBBY, and the screen only self-closes on TBD_LobbyClient.IsDeployed() which the server-side wave never sets. PREDICTED TO BE THE FIRST THING VISIBLE on the first live test after the Workbench rdb pass and before the m_bAutoDeploy flip — i.e. exactly the sequence the program doc prescribes. Fix EITHER by flipping m_bAutoDeploy in the same sitting as the rdb pass, OR by having the initial raise skip a player who already controls an entity.

T-181.30.notes: Small truth-in-comments + hardening from the wave-3 verifier. (1) TBD_MissionBrowser.c:13-20 claims 'two blocks are measured to compile and interoperate; three are not' — a THIRD modded SCR_PlayerController block (TBD_LobbyController.c:29) landed in the same wave, so the comment now misinforms. The verifier proved all three merge statically with a negative-controlled probe. (2) TBD_BriefingData.c:231 assigns m_sFactionKey without Sanitise() while every neighbouring field sanitises. (3) TBD_AdminService audit: NoteDeniedAccess takes a ring slot per (playerId,surface) and one client reaches ~5 surfaces, so ~10 unauthorised clients still evict every real action from the 60-entry ring; s_mDeniedSeen is a never-reset static. (4) Unbounded console warn per refused RPC (no data leak, log volume only). || WAVE-4 VERIFIER ADDITIONS (all MINOR, all in Gamemode/**): (1) TBD_SpawnManager.c:334-343 EnsureConnectEpoch breaks the invariant its own comment at :311-320 states — it mints a NON-ZERO epoch for any id including a departed one, so 'an unknown id fails the check' does not hold; ScheduleDeployRetry is public. Not exploitable in the shipped config (RedeployAfterDeath unreachable with m_bOneLife=1) but the guard's stated property is false, plus a small unbounded leak of epochs for ids that never disconnect. Fix: mint only when GetPlayerController(playerId) exists. (2) TBD_SpawnManager.c:1105-1110 the duplicate-audit swallow keys on m_mBindKeyCache, which non-audit paths write — the LOBBY wave calls IsPlayerDead on every registered player 250 ms after LOBBY entry, caching an identity for a player not yet audited, whose genuine audit is then swallowed: no forced epoch bump, no LogJoinVerdict, no ReclaimDepartedSeat, and m_mSeenKeys never learns them so a later reconnect logs FIRST. (3) TBD_FrameworkManager.c:193-194 vs 210 m_sLastStageRefusal is stale-readable: SetStage clears it AFTER the 'same stage' early-out, so any later no-op stage command replays an old refusal as if current. (4) TBD_SafestartManager.c:326,498 the stale-static landmine GetInstance() deliberately defends against is re-imported through both its dependencies (TBD_FrameworkManager.GetInstance and TBD_SpawnManager.GetInstance are plain constructor-set statics). Both stale directions happen to fail safe; the asymmetry is unintentional. (5) Safestart has no admin-MENU surface — TBD_EAdminAction has RESPAWN/DEPLOY/STAGE_ADVANCE only, so 'is damage off right now' is answerable only from chat. (6) Safestart layer-2 projectile sink is runtime-unverifiable: RegisterScriptHandler binds by STRING event name, so a wrong name or arity is a runtime fault no gate can see. || (7) Two more dead guards that can never fire because JsonLoadContext allocates absent nested ref fields: 'if (!mission.meta)' in TBD_MissionValidator (so 'missing meta block' is unreachable — the per-field IsEmpty checks are the real coverage) and 'if (!doc.winConditions)' in TBD_BriefingData (harmless: mode humanises to empty and endOn iterates nothing). Both are truth-in-comments issues rather than live bugs; the three that WERE live bugs were fixed when the landmine was found. || (8) '[TBD] MissionList: backend not configured' is logged at ERROR for a LEGAL state (local-file mission, no backend URL) — it is allowlisted in world-boot.sh rather than fixed. Should be WARNING or INFO. (9) TBD_SpectatorHost.HasHost's comment says it is public 'so TBD_SpawnManager can say so in its own lines' — TBD_SpawnManager never calls it; TBD_PlayAreaComponent.GetInstance() has no callers anywhere. (10) TBD_MarkerData.c:66 s_mLastLogged is a server-side static never reset on world teardown, while TBD_MarkerClient.Shutdown and TBD_MarkerIcons.ResetForWorld do reset theirs — 'statics outlive a world' is a recorded landmine and this one was missed. Bounded at 256, so cost is one suppressed log line after an in-process mission switch. (11) TBD_PlayAreaComponent.c:239-244 fails OPEN where its sibling fails closed: with a null TBD_SpawnManager it evaluates whatever the player controls, which for a spectator is the streaming host, so a dead spectator leaving the AO is told 'ONE LIFE: you will be killed'. No second death path results (KillForViolation refuses a body with no damage manager) but TBD_SpectatorHost.Tick:305-317 fails CLOSED on the identical condition and the two should agree.

T-181.31.notes: The /compiled endpoint does not validate what it serves. apps/website/api/src/handlers/missions.rs:820 calls flatten_to_mod_document and returns the result straight to the mod; contract::validate_mission_document is only ever called from #[cfg(test)] (services/mission_compile.rs:37, validate.rs:137). The write path IS guarded — validate_mission_editor_payload runs on save at :319/:587 — so the gap is specifically the read path that the game server consumes. Found by the T-181.20 fixture agent while disproving T-181.26's premise. Validate the flattened document against mission.schema.json before serving (or explain why flatten cannot produce an invalid document, which would make the mod-side sentinel work optional rather than load-bearing). Cheap, and it turns a class of runtime mod bug into a 500 at the source.

T-181.32.notes: ONE LIFE fails OPEN on a dedicated server with no backend identity (PlayerBindKey mode 3). Found by the wave-4 adversarial verifier at TBD_SpawnManager.c:2136-2141: on disconnect a 'player:<id>'-keyed death mark is DELETED, so die -> quit -> rejoin buys a fresh life unconditionally. The tell is an internal inconsistency in the SAME function — the SEAT is kept and blocked for everyone (fail-closed, reclaimable=false, :2116) while the LIFE is dropped (fail-open): two opposite answers for one key. TBD_MOD_DESIGN.md §2 sanctions durability for the listen-host name-hash case; it does NOT sanction fail-open on a dedicated server. Compounding: NoteIdentityDegraded (:1050-1056) is latched by a SINGLE session-wide bool covering both degraded modes, so one earlier mode-2 event silences the warning for the rest of the session. This is the program's #1 non-negotiable, so the fix should be a refusal to enter SAFE_START/LIVE (or at minimum a persistent banner), not a droppable log line. MUST NOT run concurrently with any other slice that owns TBD_SpawnManager.c.

T-181.33.notes: Safestart Restore must restore the PRIOR value, not force EnableDamageHandling(true). Wave-4 verifier, TBD_SafestartManager.c:522-524,595: ApplyTo never records whether a body's damage handling was already off before safestart armed, so the in-code claim that 'scope is exactly m_mHeld' limits WHICH entities are touched but not WHAT they are set to. Anything that legitimately wants damage handling off on a swept body gets it forced on at lift. Concretely collides with T-181.24's spectator dummy, which is exactly such a body. Fix: record prior state per entity in ApplyTo and restore that. Owns TBD_SafestartManager.c — must not run concurrently with any slice owning it.

T-181.34.notes: Add a container enum to mission.schema.json loadout.cargo[].container. Wave-4 verifier: the field is {type:string, minLength:1}, so a typo validates and then degrades SILENTLY at runtime to 'insert anywhere'. The authoritative four keys already exist twice in the repo — apps/website/frontend/src/arsenal_rules.rs:595 (CARGO_CONTAINERS = vest/pants/jacket/backpack) and TBD_LoadoutEquipHelper.c:814-830 (GarmentForContainer). T-181.20 added golden fixtures with correct containers, but a fixture cannot protect a vocabulary the schema does not define. Single source of truth + schema enum + a golden fixture that must fail.

T-181.35.notes: In-game identity linking — the missing half of the results contract. FOUND while briefing T-181.13.1: the backend has a complete two-step link flow (POST /api/v1/me/link creates a code for a logged-in user; POST /api/v1/ingest/link-confirm, service-token, is the GAME SERVER confirming {code, arma_id, arma_character} and is what actually sets users.arma_id — apps/website/api/src/handlers/me.rs:160-205, routes at app.rs:34-40). THE MOD IMPLEMENTS NEITHER — grep for link-confirm across Scripts/ returns nothing, and there is no #tbd link command. So outside the dev seed (dev.rs, 'dev-arma-76561190000000001') NO production user has an arma_id. Consequence: POST /ingest/match-results resolves players by 'SELECT discord_id FROM users WHERE arma_id = $1' (telemetry.rs:238), so it matches NOBODY — the POST returns success while attendance marking, user-stat recompute and leaderboard refresh all silently do nothing. That is the exact 'looks like it worked' failure this program keeps finding. Build: a player-facing chat command (e.g. '#tbd link <code>' — NOT admin-gated, every player needs it) that posts the player's durable identity from SCR_PlayerIdentityUtils.GetPlayerIdentityId plus their character name to /ingest/link-confirm, with honest handling of the backend's 404 'invalid or expired code' and 409 'arma id already linked to another account'. Whatever value is sent here MUST be byte-identical to the arma_id T-181.13.1 later sends in match-results — same accessor, ideally one shared helper, or the two halves silently disagree. Owns Backend/** + the chat surface; must not share a wave with T-181.13.1.

T-181.36.notes: golden-missions/slot-loadout-coverage.json is REJECTED by the mod at runtime — a committed fixture the server refuses to run. Caught by the new mission-seeded world-boot gate: '[TBD][Validate] ERROR slot:slot_ranger_med — kit alias ...' -> 'MISSION REJECTED — 1 error(s). The server stays in LOADING until the mission is fixed.' Cause: the fixture references kit:us_medic, which is NOT in apps/mod/tbd-framework/Data/registry.json (which knows only kit:us_ar, kit:us_rifleman, kit:us_sl, kit:us_tl, kit:sov_ar, kit:sov_rifleman, kit:sov_sl). make schema-validate passes it because mission.schema.json types `kit` as a bare string with no vocabulary — the SAME class of gap as T-181.34's cargo container. Fix is a judgement call, state it explicitly: either add a us_medic entry to the registry (if a medic kit is real) or change the fixture to an existing alias. Then close the class: the kit alias vocabulary should be checked by a gate, not discovered at mission load. NOTE this fixture is one of T-181.20's, which shipped green because the wave gate validated JSON SCHEMA only and never booted a mission.
